summary: Ifosfamide is an oxazaphosphorine nitrogen-mustard alkylating prodrug indicated, in combination with other antineoplastic agents, for third-line chemotherapy of germ-cell testicular cancer in adults. It requires hepatic CYP450 activation to its cytotoxic isophosphoramide mustard, which forms DNA cross-links causing cell death; a byproduct, acrolein, is responsible for its characteristic urotoxicity. It carries a boxed warning for severe myelosuppression (which can lead to fatal infection), encephalopathy (which may be fatal), and nephrotoxicity and urotoxicity, the latter mitigated by the prophylactic uroprotectant mesna and extensive hydration. Additional serious risks include cardiotoxicity, pulmonary toxicity, secondary malignancies, hepatic veno-occlusive disease, infertility and embryo-fetal toxicity. It is contraindicated in urinary outflow obstruction.
indications: Use in adults, in combination with certain other approved antineoplastic agents, for third-line chemotherapy of germ-cell testicular cancer

dosage.d: 1.2 grams/m2 per day by slow IV infusion over at least 30 minutes
dosage.t: Daily for 5 consecutive days; repeat every 3 weeks or after recovery from hematologic toxicity
dosage.n: Individualize dose/schedule by risk factors and adverse reactions

dosage.d: Administer mesna with ifosfamide to reduce hemorrhagic cystitis
Extensive hydration with at least 2 liters of oral or IV fluid per day

admin: Administer as a slow intravenous infusion over at least 30 minutes
Always give with the uroprotectant mesna to reduce hemorrhagic cystitis
Provide extensive hydration (at least 2 L of fluid per day) to reduce bladder toxicity
Obtain blood counts before treatment and at intervals after each cycle; monitor for CNS toxicity
Handle and prepare as a hazardous cytotoxic drug with appropriate precautions
moa: Ifosfamide is a prodrug requiring metabolic activation by hepatic cytochrome P450 isoenzymes. Hydroxylation forms unstable intermediates that decompose to the cytotoxic and urotoxic compound acrolein and the alkylating isophosphoramide mustard. The isophosphoramide mustard alkylates guanine N-7 positions in DNA, forming inter- and intra-strand cross-links that result in cell death. Acrolein, excreted in urine, is responsible for the characteristic bladder toxicity (hemorrhagic cystitis).

relative: Pre-existing severe myelosuppression / compromised bone marrow
Pre-existing CNS dysfunction or low serum albumin/bicarbonate (encephalopathy risk)
monitor: Patients on CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors
Patients with low albumin, low bicarbonate or renal impairment (encephalopathy risk)

preg: Based on its mechanism of action and human and animal data, ifosfamide can cause fetal harm when given to a pregnant woman; fetal growth retardation and neonatal anemia have been reported with ifosfamide-containing regimens, and animal studies show gene mutations, chromosomal damage, embryolethality and anomalies. Advise of the risk to a fetus; females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and after treatment, and males with female partners should also use contraception.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, women should not breastfeed during treatment with ifosfamide.
renal: Ifosfamide can cause severe nephrotoxicity, including renal failure and renal tubular damage. Monitor serum and urine chemistries; the risk of CNS and renal toxicity is increased with renal impairment. It is contraindicated in urinary outflow obstruction. Ifosfamide and its metabolites are dialyzable.
hepatic: Ifosfamide is activated by hepatic CYP450 enzymes. Hepatic veno-occlusive disease can occur. Use with monitoring; impaired hepatic metabolism may alter formation of active and neurotoxic metabolites.

major: CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St John's wort) - increase formation of active and of the neurotoxic/nephrotoxic metabolite chloroacetaldehyde; monitor for increased toxicity
Other myelosuppressive or nephrotoxic chemotherapy / radiation - additive marrow and renal toxicity
Other CNS-toxic agents (e.g. aprepitant, sedatives) - may worsen encephalopathy
moderate: CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole) - may decrease activation and reduce efficacy
Anticoagulants - increased bleeding risk with thrombocytopenia
Cisplatin - additive nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity and neurotoxicity
minor: Live vaccines - risk of disseminated infection in immunosuppressed patients
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol because of additive CNS depression and nausea.
interactions.diagnostics: Expect myelosuppression on blood counts; monitor urinalysis for hematuria and serum/urine chemistries for tubular dysfunction.

serious: Severe myelosuppression leading to fatal infections
Nephrotoxicity / renal failure and hemorrhagic cystitis
Pulmonary toxicity (interstitial pneumonitis, pulmonary fibrosis, fatal outcomes)
rare: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH)

monitoring: Complete blood count before treatment, during treatment and at intervals after each cycle
Mental status for signs of CNS toxicity/encephalopathy during and after treatment
Serum and urine chemistries and urinalysis (hematuria) for nephrotoxicity and urotoxicity
Cardiac function (ECG/clinical) in patients at risk for cardiotoxicity
Respiratory symptoms suggestive of pulmonary toxicity
Adequacy of hydration and mesna administration each cycle
counsel: This chemotherapy lowers blood counts; report fever, chills or signs of infection right away
Report confusion, drowsiness, hallucinations or unusual behavior promptly - these can signal brain toxicity
Drink plenty of fluids and take the protective medicine (mesna) as directed to protect the bladder; report blood in the urine
Avoid pregnancy and fathering a child - use effective contraception during and after treatment
Do not breastfeed during treatment; hair loss is common and usually reversible
pk: Cytotoxic effect after hepatic CYP activation to alkylating metabolites
About 7 hours at 1.6-2.4 g/m2/day; about 15 hours at higher single doses (3.8-5.0 g/m2)
Cyclical dosing (5-day courses every 3 weeks) maintains antitumor effect
Store dry product at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from temperatures above 30 C
pearls: Boxed warning: myelosuppression, encephalopathy, and nephrotoxicity/urotoxicity - all potentially fatal
Always co-administer mesna plus extensive hydration to prevent hemorrhagic cystitis (acrolein toxicity)
Encephalopathy risk rises with low albumin, low bicarbonate, renal impairment and prior cisplatin; methylene blue is used for ifosfamide encephalopathy
CYP3A4 inducers increase neurotoxic/nephrotoxic chloroacetaldehyde formation - monitor closely
missed: Ifosfamide is administered by a healthcare professional on a fixed cycle. There is no patient-managed missed dose; if a treatment appointment is missed, contact the oncology team, who will reschedule based on blood counts and cycle timing.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Serious consequences reflect dose-dependent toxicities: severe CNS toxicity, nephrotoxicity, myelosuppression and mucositis. Management is supportive - sustain the patient through the toxicity period with treatment of infection, blood-product support and other organ support. Ifosfamide and its metabolites are dialyzable, and mesna cystitis prophylaxis may help limit urotoxic effects with overdose.
